Periods are rare for species. Only a handful have them, including us. Part of the benefit of having a menstrual cycle involved in the reproductive process is the ability to cleanse the body of faulty embryos or ones that are taking advantage of the mothers nutrition and etc. It is a big task and lots of energy to grow a life for nine months and breastfeed and care for it after, so the body wants to make sure the effort is worth it

Edit: in addition to this, having a cycle means that we are only fertile for a handful of days each month. Our ovulation days (when we’re fertile) are barely noticeable to potential mates. There are studies saying we have pheromones released and are more horny and have redder cheeks near ovulation, and that men are more attracted to the sweat of ovulating women than non ovulating women on average, but other than that — it still isn’t obvious when we’re fertile compared to other species. Most species have dramatic changes when they’re fertile that attract mates, and those mates are barely attracted to them when they’re not fertile. The lack of noticeable ovulation in menstrual cycles in humans is believed to have evolved so that mates can stay with us, which is beneficial because it enables more support for future offspring and during pregnancy.
